summary: Round 4 improves ordinary post-exit classification, but it still treats `signalled is None` as proof that the evaluator was not killed. The biggest numerical risk is a caught termination exiting 255 with a crash-shaped record being charged to the model’s record budget and accepted as its result.

findings.title: Caught termination can be misclassified as a self-terminated verdict
findings.evidence: `signalled = reap.describe_exit_signal(rc)` followed by `clean_exit = signalled is None` and `if clean_exit and has_record: attempt.outcome = AttemptOutcome.EXITED`. `describe_exit_signal(255)` deliberately returns `None`.
findings.why_wrong: A configured evaluator or shell activation is user-supplied and can catch SIGTERM, write a final crash-shaped record plus a fault phrase, then exit 255. This code sees no signal, demotes the attempt to `EXITED`, and `_settle` charges the model’s `record` budget instead of the bounded ambiguity budget. The result can therefore be accepted as the model’s verdict even though termination caused the record.
findings.suggested_fix: Carry explicit runner-kill provenance on `Attempt` and never apply the demotion after a runner-initiated kill. For external or caught termination, use a generated-script signal side channel or conservatively keep the attempt ambiguous.

findings.title: Dry-run rollback is not crash-safe and can leave planning state persisted
findings.evidence: `Runner.run()` calls `state.save()` before checking `self.args.dry_run`; cleanup later restores with `state.path.write_bytes(dry_run_ledger_snapshot)` or unlinks the file.
findings.why_wrong: A SIGKILL or process failure after the pre-dry-run save leaves task entries, settlement bits, and the current config digest on disk. The next real run can then choose different SKIP/RUN/budget paths, despite the dry-run contract saying it writes nothing. The restore itself is also non-atomic.
findings.suggested_fix: Do not persist the planning ledger at all on dry-run; operate on an in-memory copy. If restoration is retained, use an atomic temporary-file replacement and make restoration failure non-successful.
